decisions.reason: A classic lever handle close to the core range costs little to carry, and one year on the market is too short for any weak results to be read as more than temporary.
A full handle family means larger investment in tooling and variants, so management would hold onto it to protect that commitment.
This handle design adds little investment beyond the core range, so dropping it would save little, and it is kept while its first-year results are still unclear.
Like C, this handle design was a small, low-visibility investment, and after one year there is not enough evidence to justify pulling it.
A lever handle family represents a substantial range investment, and management would keep it rather than write that investment off.
The L700 electronic access system was promoted publicly as unique and is central to the firm's announced move into digital building organization, so management is strongly committed to it.
